title: Lesson Plan — Laws of Motion (Class 12 NIOS Physics)
subject: Physics
objectives: State and apply Newton's three laws of motion to one-dimensional and inclined-plane problems.
Apply F = ma and F = dp/dt; compute impulse and use it to relate force, time and change of momentum.
Apply conservation of linear momentum to recoil, collisions and rocket-style problems.
Apply f_s ≤ μ_s N and f_k = μ_k N to decide whether a body slides and compute its acceleration.
Solve Atwood's-machine and inclined-plane problems with friction and tension using free-body diagrams.
materials: Two carts on a low-friction track for collision demos
Spring scale and small weights for the f = ma demo
Inclined-plane setup with a wooden block (for the angle-of-repose demo)

activities.description: Cart-collision demo: roll one cart at the other (initially at rest) and ask the class to predict the outcome (sticky vs bouncy collision). Surface the idea that 'something' is conserved.
teacher_actions: Show two collisions: sticky (e.g. velcro) and bouncy (springs).
Promise the answer is in the conservation-of-momentum section.

activities.description: Pair work: two students stand on skateboards (or chairs with wheels) and push off each other. They observe their relative speeds and link the result to mass.
teacher_actions: Demo or describe the skateboard activity safely.
Ask: 'If one student is twice as heavy, does she move twice as fast or half as fast?'
student_actions: Argue for the m₁ v₁ = m₂ v₂ pattern.

activities.description: Direct instruction: (i) define force and inertia and the newton; (ii) state Newton's three laws with one demo each; (iii) derive conservation of momentum from the third law for two interacting bodies; (iv) introduce static and kinetic friction with the angle-of-repose demo; (v) work the Atwood-machine result.
teacher_actions: Demo the cart collision and quantify with masses written on the board.
Tilt the inclined plane until the block slips; record the angle and compute μ_s = tan θ.
Solve Atwood's machine for a and T on the board.
student_actions: Predict the angle of repose before measurement.
Add the standard Atwood formulas a = (m₁−m₂)g/(m₁+m₂) and T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁+m₂) to a 'rules box'.

activities.description: Application station: six problems — F = ma with a single body, impulse / Δp on a bouncing ball, recoil, inelastic collision, friction-on-a-floor, frictionless inclined plane.
teacher_actions: Pair fast finishers with slower ones.
Collect common mistakes for the Evaluate phase.
student_actions: Work problems individually with full free-body diagrams.
Ask a peer before asking the teacher.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 8 items drawn from the chapter's question bank — at least one MCQ on each law, one on impulse, one on friction, one on momentum conservation, and one short-answer on Newton's third law.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit-ticket; remind students it is individual work.
Address top two miss items in 4 minutes.
student_actions: Self-mark and reflect on missed items.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE-level prompt ('Construct a real-world scenario in which Newton's third law explains the motion (other than walking, recoil and rocket)'). Preview the next chapter (Motion in a Plane) by mentioning projectile motion.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and CREATE prompt.

homework: Complete the rest of the Worksheet — Laws of Motion.
Complete one CREATE-level question on Newton's third law.
Solve one connected-body problem (block + hanging mass over a pulley) including friction, tension and acceleration.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question MCQ + 2 long-answer quiz from the chapter's bank for the next class.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the bullet-and-block momentum problem using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the angle-of-repose derivation.
references: NIOS Senior Secondary Physics, Module 1, Lesson 3: Laws of Motion.
NCERT Class 11 Physics, Chapter 5: Laws of Motion.
